cemc-gauss7-2002-01.title: Sort them
cemc-gauss7-2002-01.body:
In order: $0, 1, 3, 5, 8$. The middle (third) number is $3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

cemc-gauss7-2002-03.title: Add top and bottom first
cemc-gauss7-2002-03.body:
Numerator: $2 + 1 = 3$. Denominator: $7 + 6 = 13$. So the value is $\frac{3}{13}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{3}{13}$**

cemc-gauss7-2002-05.title: Earn, then add
cemc-gauss7-2002-05.body:
She earns $7 \times \$5 = \$35$. Her account then holds $\$20 + \$35 = \$55$.

**Answer: (D) \$55**

cemc-gauss7-2002-06.title: Shortest time wins
cemc-gauss7-2002-06.body:
The winner is the rat with the **shortest** time, i.e. the shortest bar. Devon's bar is the shortest (about 6.5 seconds).

**Answer: (D) Devon**

cemc-gauss7-2002-07.title: Use symmetry
cemc-gauss7-2002-07.body:
The numbers are evenly spaced, so the mean is halfway between the middle two: halfway between 14 and 16 is 15.

**Answer: (E) 15**

cemc-gauss7-2002-08.title: Evaluate each
cemc-gauss7-2002-08.body:
$P + Q = 3$, $P \times Q = 2$, $\frac PQ = \frac12$, $\frac QP = 2$, $P^Q = 1^2 = 1$. Only $\frac12$ is not an integer.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{P}{Q}$**

cemc-gauss7-2002-09.title: Cut into sixteenths
cemc-gauss7-2002-09.body:
$\frac34 = \frac{12}{16}$. Sharing 12 sixteenths among 4 friends gives each $\frac{3}{16}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{3}{16}$**

cemc-gauss7-2002-10.title: Find the side
cemc-gauss7-2002-10.body:
Each square has side 5 cm (since $5 \times 5 = 25$). Side by side they make a 10 cm by 5 cm rectangle, with perimeter $2 \times (10 + 5) = 30$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 30 cm**

cemc-gauss7-2002-10.title: Count square sides
cemc-gauss7-2002-10.body:
The rectangle's outline consists of 6 sides of the small squares (the shared side is inside). $6 \times 5 = 30$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 30 cm**

cemc-gauss7-2002-11.title: Quarter of the race
cemc-gauss7-2002-11.body:
25% is one quarter. If one quarter is 50 m, the whole race is $4 \times 50 = 200$ m.

**Answer: (C) 200**

cemc-gauss7-2002-12.title: Step by step
cemc-gauss7-2002-12.body:
Jack is $19 - 6 = 13$. Doug is 3 years older than Jack: $13 + 3 = 16$.

**Answer: (B) 16**

cemc-gauss7-2002-12.title: Compare directly
cemc-gauss7-2002-12.body:
Qaddama is 6 years older than Jack and Doug is 3 years older than Jack, so Qaddama is 3 years older than Doug. Doug is $19 - 3 = 16$.

**Answer: (B) 16**

cemc-gauss7-2002-13.title: Find the next palindrome
cemc-gauss7-2002-13.body:
A four-digit palindrome starting with 2 has the form $2aa2$. After 2002 the next one is 2112. So we add $2112 - 2002 = 110$.

**Answer: (B) 110**

cemc-gauss7-2002-13.title: Check the choices
cemc-gauss7-2002-13.body:
$2002 + 11 = 2013$, $2002 + 18 = 2020$, $2002 + 108 = 2110$: not palindromes. $2002 + 110 = 2112$ is a palindrome, and it is the smallest choice that works ($1001$ is bigger).

**Answer: (B) 110**

cemc-gauss7-2002-14.title: Compute each
cemc-gauss7-2002-14.body:
- BEEF: $18$
- FADE: $6 + 1 + 4 + 5 = 16$
- FEED: $6 + 5 + 5 + 4 = 20$
- FACE: $6 + 1 + 3 + 5 = 15$
- DEAF: $4 + 5 + 1 + 6 = 16$

FEED has the greatest value.

**Answer: (C) FEED**

cemc-gauss7-2002-14.title: Compare to BEEF
cemc-gauss7-2002-14.body:
FEED and BEEF share the letters E, E, F. FEED has D (4) where BEEF has B (2), so FEED $= 18 + 2 = 20$. FADE and DEAF use the same letters (A, D, E, F), worth $16$, and FACE has C instead of D, worth $15$. So FEED is largest.

**Answer: (C) FEED**

cemc-gauss7-2002-15.title: Base and height
cemc-gauss7-2002-15.body:
The shaded triangle is $ACD$. Its base is $CD = BD - BC = 10 - 3 = 7$ and its height is $AC = 4$ (perpendicular to $BD$).

Area $= \frac12 \times 7 \times 4 = 14$.

**Answer: (A) 14**

cemc-gauss7-2002-15.title: Subtract triangles
cemc-gauss7-2002-15.body:
Triangle $ABD$ has area $\frac12 \times 10 \times 4 = 20$. Triangle $ABC$ has area $\frac12 \times 3 \times 4 = 6$. The shaded part is $20 - 6 = 14$.

**Answer: (A) 14**

cemc-gauss7-2002-17.title: Angle sum, then straight line
cemc-gauss7-2002-17.body:
The angles of the triangle are $2x$, $3x$ and $x$, so $6x = 180$ and $x = 30$.

The angles $x^\circ$ and $z^\circ$ lie on a straight line, so $z = 180 - 30 = 150$.

**Answer: (A) 150**

cemc-gauss7-2002-17.title: Exterior angle
cemc-gauss7-2002-17.body:
The exterior angle $z$ equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: $z = 2x + 3x = 5x$. Since $6x = 180$, $x = 30$ and $z = 150$.

**Answer: (A) 150**

cemc-gauss7-2002-19.title: Count the endings
cemc-gauss7-2002-19.body:
Each missing digit can be any of 0–9, so the two-digit ending can be 00, 01, …, 99: $10 \times 10 = 100$ possibilities. In the worst case she must try all of them.

**Answer: (A) 100**

cemc-gauss7-2002-20.title: Follow each step
cemc-gauss7-2002-20.body:
**Rotate $180^\circ$:** the word moves from below the origin to above it and is turned upside down (letters in reverse order and each letter upside down).

**Reflect in the $x$-axis:** it flips back below the axis. Flipping an upside-down word top-to-bottom leaves it right side up but **mirrored left-to-right**.

So the final image is the mirror image of "stop" below the axis: the letters appear in the order p, o, t, s, each reversed, which looks like "qoʇz". That is picture (E).

**Answer: (E)**

cemc-gauss7-2002-20.title: Combine the moves
cemc-gauss7-2002-20.body:
A $180^\circ$ rotation followed by a reflection in the $x$-axis is the same as a single reflection in the $y$-axis. Reflecting "stop" in the $y$-axis keeps it below the axis and mirrors it left-to-right, which is picture (E).

**Answer: (E)**

cemc-gauss7-2002-21.title: Count new handshakes
cemc-gauss7-2002-21.body:
The first person shakes 4 hands, the second 3 new ones, then 2, then 1: $4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10$.

**Answer: (B) 10**

cemc-gauss7-2002-21.title: Count and halve
cemc-gauss7-2002-21.body:
Each of the 5 people shakes 4 hands: $5 \times 4 = 20$. Every handshake was counted twice (once for each person), so there are $20 \div 2 = 10$.

**Answer: (B) 10**

cemc-gauss7-2002-22.title: Find the dimensions
cemc-gauss7-2002-22.body:
From the net, the prism measures 10 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Its surface area is
$$2(10 \times 6) + 2(10 \times 5) + 2(6 \times 5) = 120 + 100 + 60 = 280 \text{ cm}^2.$$

**Answer: (C) 280**

cemc-gauss7-2002-22.title: Add up the net
cemc-gauss7-2002-22.body:
The surface area is just the area of the net. The middle strip is 6 cm tall and $5 + 10 + 5 + 10 = 30$ cm long: $180$. The two flaps are 10 cm by 5 cm: $2 \times 50 = 100$. Total: $280$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: (C) 280**

cemc-gauss7-2002-23.title: Find the new total
cemc-gauss7-2002-23.body:
Black or gold: $3 + 6 = 9$ marbles. If $\frac{9}{\text{total}} = \frac37$, then the total is 21 (since $\frac{9}{21} = \frac37$).

The bag had $3 + 6 + 2 + 6 = 17$ marbles, so Mark added $21 - 17 = 4$ white marbles.

**Answer: (D) 4**

cemc-gauss7-2002-23.title: Test the choices
cemc-gauss7-2002-23.body:
With $w$ white marbles the probability is $\frac{9}{17 + w}$. For $w = 4$: $\frac{9}{21} = \frac37$. ✓

**Answer: (D) 4**

cemc-gauss7-2002-24.title: Trapezoid formula
cemc-gauss7-2002-24.body:
Triangle $XSR$ has base $SR = 8$ and height 8. Since $Y$ and $Z$ are midpoints of $XS$ and $XR$, segment $YZ$ is parallel to $SR$, half its length ($YZ = 4$), and halfway up (height 4 above $SR$).

Area of $YZRS = \frac12 (8 + 4) \times 4 = 24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

cemc-gauss7-2002-24.title: Subtract the small triangle
cemc-gauss7-2002-24.body:
Triangle $XSR$ has area $\frac12 \times 8 \times 8 = 32$. Triangle $XYZ$ is a half-size copy, so its area is $\frac14 \times 32 = 8$. The trapezoid is $32 - 8 = 24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

cemc-gauss7-2002-25.title: Find the digit sets
cemc-gauss7-2002-25.body:
We need three digits (each 1–9) with product 24. The possible sets are
$$\{1, 3, 8\},\ \{1, 4, 6\},\ \{2, 3, 4\},\ \{2, 2, 6\}.$$
(No digit can be 0, and 24 has no other split into three digits.)

- Each set of three different digits can be arranged in $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ ways: $3 \times 6 = 18$ numbers.
- $\{2, 2, 6\}$ gives only 3 numbers: 226, 262, 622.

Total: $18 + 3 = 21$.

**Answer: (E) 21**
